hero.title: Part Load Transport
intro: Flexible transport for smaller and recurring industrial consignments that do not require an entire vehicle.

sections.title: Part Load Transport at a glance
Consolidated movement for smaller industrial loads.
sections.subtitle: Share the operating details.
intro: Part Load Transport combines compatible accepted consignments moving through the network. It helps businesses move smaller quantities without booking the full carrying capacity of a vehicle.

The operating plan considers packaging, cargo compatibility, route, handling requirements and delivery instructions. Transit and delivery timing can differ from dedicated FTL because the movement is consolidated.

cards.title: What this service can include
list: Consolidated movement for smaller accepted consignments

Recurring factory and distributor dispatch coordination
Godown and door-delivery arrangements where available
Freight Paid, To Pay or agreed account billing

sections.title: Frequently asked questions.
intro: These answers explain the usual planning approach. Share the exact cargo and route for a shipment-specific response.

faqs.a: Part Load Transport, also called PTL, consolidates compatible consignments so a customer can move a smaller load without booking a complete vehicle.

faqs.q: What packaging can be considered for PTL?
faqs.a: Depending on cargo acceptance and route, PTL may include properly packaged drums, carboys, cartons, bags, pallets and other industrial packages.

faqs.q: Can PTL be delivered Door to Door?
faqs.a: Door-to-Door, Godown-to-Door and Godown-to-Godown arrangements may be available depending on the route, destination and agreed booking terms.

faqs.q: How is PTL different from FTL?
faqs.a: PTL shares network capacity with compatible freight, while FTL allocates a dedicated vehicle to one accepted consignment.
